chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Al-Husayn ibn Mayyah, from Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Beware of inter-mingling with the lowly people (rif-raff), for the lowly do not lead to the goodness.

key_terms.السَّفِلَةِ: The lowly, common people, or those of lower moral standing

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by 'lowly people' in the context of social interaction?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns against close companionship with *al-safala*, a term Shia scholars often interpret not merely as the general populace but as those lacking spiritual refinement or moral depth. This advice underscores the principle of *al-wala' wa al-barra'* (alliance and disavowal), emphasizing that prolonged association with the morally lowly can dilute one's own spiritual standing and hinder the pursuit of excellence (*ihsan*).
